name: שֹׁמֵר
summary: Two bear the name. One is an Asherite, son of Heber and brother of Japhlet and Hotham (1Ch 7:32), called Shemer in 1Ch 7:34. The other is the parent of Jehozabad, one of the two servants who struck down Joash king of Judah (2Ki 12:22); Chronicles names that parent Shimrith the Moabitess (2Ch 24:26), a feminine name of the same root. The name is the qal participle of שָׁמַר used as a noun, the ordinary word for a keeper or watchman (Gen 4:9; Isa 21:11), and may be short for a name such as Shemariah, “Yahweh has kept”.

evidence.note: “Heber begot Japhlet and שׁוֹמֵר and Hotham, and Shua their sister.”
“Jozabad son of Shimeath and Jehozabad son of שֹׁמֵר, his servants, struck him and he died.”
The same conspirator is “Jehozabad son of שִׁמְרִית the Moabitess”.
The word the name is: הֲשֹׁמֵר אָחִי אָנֹכִי, “am I my brother's keeper?”

note: 2Ki 12:22 is 12:21 in English numbering (TIPNR key Shomer@2Ki.12.21, which TIPNR also uses for Shimrith of 2Ch 24:26, treating the two as one person). BDB's v.ef.ad is counted by spelling, so nearly all its tokens are the common participle שֹׁמֵר of the verb (v.ef.aa); the name itself is only 2Ki 12:22 and 1Ch 7:32. Punic has the same participle as a title and ŠMR as a short name (Krahmalkov p. 470).
